options.label: A

explanation: Average product is total output divided by workers: 100/5 = 20 units per worker.

explanation: A positive marginal product means the added worker produces additional output. Total product therefore rises.

reference: PRD-1.A | PRD-1.A.1-3 | Skill 1.A/1.C/2.C as applicable Quality-Control Audits Audit 1 — CED Alignment and Scope All 100 questions are confined to Topic 3.1, PRD-1.A, with primary emphasis on PRD-1.A.1 through PRD-1.A.3: the input-output relationship represented by the production function, marginal and average product, and diminishing marginal returns. The bank also uses the short-run/long-run distinction only to the extent necessary to interpret the production function: in the short run at least one input is fixed; in the long run firms can vary all inputs. No question requires short-run cost curves, marginal cost, average fixed/variable/total cost, long-run average total cost, economies of scale, profit maximization, perfect competition, or any later Unit 3 topic. Graph questions use only the production-function relationships among total product, marginal product, and average product, consistent with the CED production-function visual. Audit 2 — Construction, Difficulty, and Answer Integrity Question count: 100 unique stems. Difficulty distribution: 30 Easy, 40 Medium, 30 Hard. Each question has five answer choices (A–E) with exactly one keyed answer. Correct-answer distribution is balanced at 20 each for A, B, C, D, and E. Easy items emphasize definitions and one-step MP/AP calculations. Medium items combine production tables, short-run reasoning, and relationships among TP, MP, and AP. Hard items require multi-step reconstruction of missing production values, comparison across firms, and integrated interpretation of diminishing marginal returns. All numerical items were recomputed during generation. Marginal product is calculated from changes in total product; average product equals total product divided by units of the variable input; total product reaches a maximum when marginal product is zero and falls when marginal product is negative.
